name: skills
description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
one_liner: A collection of ready-made 'playbooks' that teach AI coding assistants how to work the way an experienced engineer would, like asking clarifying questions before writing code.
buyer: A freelance developer or small dev shop that wants their AI coding assistant to produce less bloated, more aligned code without writing their own prompt-engineering playbooks from scratch.
business_use_cases: A dev agency installs these skills across every client project so junior developers and AI assistants both produce more consistent, reviewed code.
A coding bootcamp licenses a customized version of the skill set to teach students how to work effectively with AI coding tools.
A solo freelancer uses the 'grill-me'-style skill to run better client intake conversations, reducing scope creep on fixed-price projects.

money_ideas.idea: The author already monetizes this via a newsletter and courses around AI-assisted engineering; others could do the same by publishing a specialized skill pack for a niche stack.

steal_this: This is free, open, developer-only tooling that mainly drives newsletter signups and reputation for its author — a good lead-magnet format to copy for your own niche, not something to resell directly.
